name: Vitaly Orlov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Vitaly Orlov is the CEO and cofounder of Norebo Holding, the largest vertically integrated seafood company in Russia.
In the late 1990s, Orlov and two partners, who he later bought out, started a business buying used fishing trawlers then exchanged for fish in Russia.
Over the years, Norebo has spent $600 million to acquire fishing companies in the North and Far East of Russia.
Today Norebo, which operates 15 companies, catches 400,000 tons of cod, haddock and pollock a year in the Norwegian Sea, Barents Sea and the Far East.
forbes_facts: Orlov moved to Norway in 1996 and lived there until 2014. He gave up his Norwegian citizenship when he moved back to Murmansk, Russia.

name: Huxiong Chen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023-2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026); Hurun China (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: Chen Huxiong is the vice chairman and president of Shanghai M&G Stationary Inc.
M&G Stationary was founded in 1996.
Chen's brother Chen Huwen is M&G's chairman and a fellow billionaire.

name: Lia Maria Aguiar
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2019); Hurun Global (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Lia Maria Aguiar inherited a banking fortune from her late father, Amador Aguiar, the founder of Bradesco, one of Brazil's largest banks.
Lia Aguiar and her twin sister Lina were adopted by Bradesco founder Amador Aguiar after being abandoned in front of a Bradesco branch in Sao Paulo.
Aguiar fought a long court battle over her father's will with his second wife, whom he married less than five months before his death.
Aguiar also owns shares of Bradespar, the bank's non-financial arm, which is publicly traded and specializes in industrial investments.
forbes_facts: In 2008, Aguiar started her own foundation, Lia Maria Aguiar Foundation, to support the city of Campos do Jordao, where she has been living since the early 1990s.

name: Xu Shaochun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun China (2007-2026)
forbes_bio: Xu Shaochun chairs Kingdee, one of China's largest homegrown software companies.
Xu holds a degree in computer science from Southwest University.
He also holds a master's degree in accounting from the Chinese Academy of Fiscal Sciences, as well as an executive MBA from the China Europe International Business School.

name: Soichiro Minami
forbes_bio: Soichiro Minami founded and runs Visional, a job search and human resources software firm.
U.S.-educated Minami, founded the firm in 2009 after working for Morgan Stanley and Japanese e-commerce giant Rakuten, founded by billionaire Hiroshi Mikitani.
In April 2021, Minami listed the firm on the Tokyo Stock Exchange's bourse for startups, Mothers.
Visional posted over $380 million in revenue in the fiscal year ended in July 2023.
forbes_facts: Minami has a double degree in economics and international relations from Tufts University.
In 2004, he helped Rakuten set up its professional baseball team, the Rakuten Golden Eagles.

name: Anant Asavabhokhin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2021-2024); Hurun Global (2023-2024)
forbes_bio: Thai property tycoon Anant Asavabhokin's biggest asset is a stake in SET-listed Land And Houses.
He founded the company with his mother, Piangjai Harnpanij, in 1983. The company is known for its focus on detached houses.
In 2021, the company acquired SpringHill Suites by Marriott, a 120-rooom hotel in California for $31 million.
In March 2024, the company acquired the 176-room Residence Inn Manhattan Beach, a hotel in Los Angeles, near Disneyland, for $68 million.
forbes_facts: In 2017, he resigned from the chairmanship of four of his companies over money laundering charges. He denied any wrongdoing.
The Covid-19 pandemic hit the company's rental income but saw an increase in the sale of semi-detached houses and townhouses.

name: Guido Barilla
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2016-2018); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Guido Barilla is the chairman of Barilla, and the fourth-generation heir to the pasta fortune that he shares with his three billionaire siblings.
Barilla is the largest pasta company in the world with an estimated $4 billion in annual revenue.
Barilla has grown by acquiring companies in France, Turkey and Greece; it also has two pasta plants in the U.S.
The business was founded in 1877 in Parma, Italy.
The family sold out to American firm W.R. Grace in 1971 but Pietro Barilla, Guido's father, bought it back eight years later.

name: Chen Baohua
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2023); Hurun Global (2018-2023); Hurun China (2006-2026)
forbes_bio: Chen Baohua is general manager of Shanghai-listed Zhejiang Huahai Pharmaceutical, a pharmaceuticals supplier.
Chen holds a degree in chemical analysis from the Zhejiang University of Technology.
After graduation, he worked at a state-run pharmaceuticals factory.
In 1989, Chen quit and cofounded the predecessor of Huahai in the eastern Chinese city of Linhaiat with less than $3,000; he was only 29 years old.
